counter_evidence:
I measured this on the dev box. Each run was a fresh node process: Node 24.22.1, node:sqlite 3.53.4, a WAL index, and synthetic canonical-JSON journals of about 0.7 KB per event. The journals use the winning events/<aa>/<sha>.json fan-out, with a flat layout for comparison. Scripts and data are in C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-User-Documents-projects-EMS-workshop1--claude-worktrees-knowledge-store-research-9c609c\f3bbe503-2a20-4258-976b-7d457d3bf63a\scratchpad\bench\c4r-q8z.

(1) Single uncontended call, full check (readdir of the root plus 256 subdirs, SELECT id FROM event into a Set, two-way set difference, sha256 over the sorted names compared with the stored digest), 31 runs, measured twice. At 5k fanned out the median was 24.3 / 25.0 ms (max 36). At 20k fanned out it was 63.7 / 61.8 ms (max 81). At 5k flat it was 13.6 ms. Readdir alone at 5k flat was 5.2 ms, which matches Proposal D's 5.96 ms. So D measured a flat readdir only. Fan-out was added later by judge-3 (judge-3.md:329), and fan-out plus the SELECT, diff and digest make the real check about 4x D's figure. Within that single-call case the bounds hold.

(2) Concurrent calls, read-only check. With 8 at once at 5k, the medians were 49.1 and 51.6 ms (p90 52.7 and 56.3). With 4 at once at 5k, the median was 55.4 ms. That is a measured median above 50 ms. At 20k with 8 or 4 at once the medians were 113 and 119 ms, still under 200. Readdir slows from 17 ms to about 40 ms under contention.

(3) D's write path runs the check inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. architect-D.md:194 has step (2) BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then (3) readdir. Every lookup is a write, because it appends lookup.performed (architect-D.md:167,284). A lookup-shaped write (lock, check, temp+rename, insert, commit) with 8 at once gave these results. At 5k: lock wait median 65 ms, p90 266 ms; end-to-end median 98 ms, p90 294 ms, max 462 ms. At 20k: lock wait median 199 ms, p90 647 ms; end-to-end median 261 ms, p90 728 ms, max 811 ms. The check is correct throughout (missing=0, extra=0, digest ok). But the queued latency per call breaks the 200 ms bound.

(4) If the digest is read as hashing file contents, the medians are 472 ms at 5k and 1,690 ms at 20k, 10x over the bounds.

(5) The falsifier's premise does not hold on this box. Defender is off: Get-MpComputerStatus shows RealTimeProtectionEnabled False and AMRunningMode Not running, and WinDefend and WdFilter are Stopped. The active antivirus is 360 Total Security: SecurityCenter2 lists it, QHActiveDefense is Running, and the 360FsFlt and 360AvFlt filter drivers are Running. All the numbers above were taken under 360's filter.

(6) NTFS fan-out is not pathological. 256 readdirs over 20k files took a median of 30 ms.
trace:
Cost of the check against the claim's bounds, per case:
- Single uncontended call: 25 ms at 5k (bound 50) and 62 ms at 20k (bound 200). Inside the bounds.
- 4 or 8 concurrent read-only checks: 49 to 55 ms at 5k, on or over the 50 ms bound.
- 8 concurrent lookups through D's write path at 20k: end-to-end median 261 ms, over the 200 ms bound, because the check runs inside the write lock and the calls queue on it.
- Content hashing: 0.47 s at 5k and 1.7 s at 20k, so the check fails if the digest reads file contents.

What survives is that a check over file names only, run outside the write lock, needs no daemon, watcher or hook.
narrowed_claim:
A per-call freshness check needs no daemon, watcher or hook, on four conditions:
1. It reads directory entries only: readdir of events/ and its 256 fan-out subdirectories, plus a sha256 over the sorted id names compared with a digest stored in the index. File contents are read only when a new file is ingested.
2. It runs outside the BEGIN IMMEDIATE write transaction, or keeps only a cheap re-check inside the lock.
3. The journal holds about 20k events or fewer.
4. The bounds are met for an uncontended call on this box under its actual antivirus, which is 360 Total Security's filter drivers; Defender is off. The measured medians were about 25 ms at 5k and 62 ms at 20k fanned out.

With 4 to 8 simultaneous agent calls, the 5k median rises to 49 to 55 ms and the 20k median to about 115 ms. If the check stays inside the write lock, as D's step 3 has it, 8 concurrent lookups at 20k give a median of 261 ms and a p90 of 728 ms. A first call with a cold cache after a reboot was not measured.

Proposal D's 5.96 ms figure is a flat-directory readdir alone and does not represent the design as adopted.
what_would_settle_it: Not applicable, because the verdict is NARROWED. Two things remain unmeasured: the first call with a cold file-system cache after a reboot, and behaviour with Defender's real-time protection on instead of 360 Total Security. To settle them, rerun scratchpad/bench/c4r-q8z/scripts/run.mjs and parw.mjs once right after a reboot, and once more if the owner ever switches antivirus.
design_consequence:
1. Pin the digest as sha256 over the sorted event-id names, never over file contents. Validate content against the hash only when a new file is ingested; the full content check belongs in fsck and rebuild.
2. Move the freshness readdir, set difference and ingest out of BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Do the check first, then take the lock and only re-confirm a cheap marker (the stored digest or count) before the append. This keeps the lock held for about 6 ms instead of 30 to 70 ms. Without it, concurrent lookups queue: every lookup is a write, because it appends lookup.performed.
3. Check the digest first, and run SELECT id plus the set difference only when the digest does not match. That saves about 20 to 28 ms at 20k.
4. Replace the 5.96 ms figure in the register with fanned-out numbers measured with concurrency. The KS build should add a node:test benchmark at 5k and 20k events, with 8 concurrent callers, that asserts the latency budget.
5. Event count grows with lookup.performed, not with the number of entries, so the 20k ceiling can be reached within the plan. The cost scales roughly linearly, about 3 ms per 1,000 events uncontended. Set a compaction or rollup trigger, or switch to stat-based change detection on the subdirectories, before the journal passes about 20k events.
6. Doctor and the docs should name 360 Total Security, not Defender, as the antivirus on the box.
